entities.name: PMID:27506406
observations: A 67-case human clival chordoma study compared Type I limited versus Type II more serious dural penetration.

Greater dural penetration correlated with worse overall survival and progression-free survival; Type I had longer mean overall survival and, after total resection, longer mean progression-free survival.
Type II tumors showed higher PDGFR-β/PDGFRB expression than Type I tumors; assays included immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blotting.
The reported associations do not establish that PDGFRB causes dural invasion or poor outcome.

entities.name: PMID:32533822
observations: A 12-patient human chordoma study compared tumors with versus without dural penetration and found broad differential lncRNA/mRNA expression involving invasion-related pathways.
The available report did not provide PDGFRB-specific expression or survival statistics, so it does not independently confirm the PDGFRB-prognosis association.

entities.name: Clival chordoma
observations: The key comparative study assessed dural penetration, prognosis, and PDGFR-β expression in human clival chordomas.

entities.name: PDGFRB
observations: PDGFRB encodes platelet-derived growth factor receptor beta; higher expression was reported in more seriously dural-penetrating Type II clival chordomas than Type I tumors in a 67-case cohort.
The evidence supports association with invasive phenotype, not causality.
